title: YouTube Intelligence Pro Input
description: Pull YouTube with rich enrichment. Mix search terms, video URLs, channel handles, playlists, video IDs, hashtag URLs, and shorts URLs. Each video ships as one dataset row.

searchTerms.title: Search terms
searchTerms.description: YouTube search queries. Each term runs an independent search. Combine with sortBy, uploadDate, duration, and features filters below.

startUrls.title: YouTube URLs
startUrls.description: Mix any of: video URL (/watch?v= or youtu.be/), channel URL (/@handle, /channel/UC..., /c/, /user/), playlist URL (/playlist?list=), shorts URL (/shorts/), hashtag URL (/hashtag/), or search results URL (/results?search_query=).

videoIds.title: Direct video IDs
videoIds.description: 11 character YouTube video IDs (e.g. dQw4w9WgXcQ). Fastest input mode. Skip the listing crawl and fetch each video directly.

channelHandles.title: Channel handles
channelHandles.description: Channel handles like @MrBeast or @veritasium. Pulls the channel's video catalog up to maxVideosPerChannel. Combine with dateFrom or dateTo to slice the catalog by upload date.

maxVideosPerSearch.title: Max videos per search term
maxVideosPerSearch.description: Cap on regular videos returned per search. 0 means everything YouTube exposes (typically up to a few hundred).

maxShortsPerSearch.title: Max shorts per search term
maxShortsPerSearch.description: Cap on shorts returned per search. 0 disables shorts in search results.

maxStreamsPerSearch.title: Max live streams per search term
maxStreamsPerSearch.description: Cap on live streams returned per search. 0 disables live results.

maxVideosPerChannel.title: Max videos per channel
maxVideosPerChannel.description: Cap on videos pulled per channel handle or channel URL. Older catalogs scroll deep, so this is the safest knob to control cost.

maxVideosPerPlaylist.title: Max videos per playlist
maxVideosPerPlaylist.description: Cap on videos pulled per playlist URL.

uploadDate.title: Upload date filter
uploadDate.description: Restrict search results by recency. Applies to searchTerms only.

duration.title: Duration filter
duration.description: Restrict search results by length. Applies to searchTerms only.

sortBy.title: Sort search results
sortBy.description: Sort order for searchTerms. Default is relevance.

features.title: Feature filters
features.description: Restrict search to videos with these features. Multiple values stack. Applies to searchTerms only.

dateFrom.title: Date from (channel + playlist scraping)
dateFrom.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Drops videos uploaded before this date when crawling channels or playlists. Leave blank for no lower bound.

dateTo.title: Date to (channel + playlist scraping)
dateTo.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Drops videos uploaded after this date when crawling channels or playlists. Leave blank for no upper bound.

extractTranscript.title: Download transcript
extractTranscript.description: Pull the auto generated or human written transcript. Each segment carries start time, duration, and text. Useful for AI summarization, content audits, and SEO research.

transcriptLanguages.title: Transcript languages
transcriptLanguages.description: Preferred transcript language codes in priority order (e.g. en, es, de, ja, hi). The first available track is used. Leave default to take whatever YouTube serves first.

extractTopComments.title: Extract top comments
extractTopComments.description: Pull the top comments thread. Each comment carries author, channel ID, text, like count, reply count, posted time, and pinned or hearted flag.

maxComments.title: Max comments per video
maxComments.description: Cap on top level comments returned per video. Ignored if extractTopComments is off.

extractCommentReplies.title: Extract comment replies
extractCommentReplies.description: Walk into each top level comment and pull the first batch of replies. Adds latency. Off by default.

extractChapters.title: Extract chapters
extractChapters.description: Pull the chapter timeline if the creator added one (or YouTube auto generated one). Each chapter has title, start time, and thumbnail.

extractRelatedVideos.title: Extract related videos
extractRelatedVideos.description: Pull the up next sidebar (video ID, title, channel, view count). Useful for content recommendation graphs.

extractChannelStats.title: Enrich with channel stats
extractChannelStats.description: Resolve subscriber count, total video count, joined date, country, and links for every distinct channel encountered. One extra page hit per channel.

extractMusicAndCredits.title: Extract music tracks and credits
extractMusicAndCredits.description: Pull the music tracks panel (song title, artist, album, license) and the credit list (people, locations) if present.

extractMostReplayed.title: Extract most replayed heatmap
extractMostReplayed.description: Pull the most replayed segment markers (timestamp + intensity 0 to 1). Lets analysts find the highest engagement moments programmatically.

extractStreamUrls.title: Extract direct stream URLs
extractStreamUrls.description: Capture available video and audio stream URLs and bitrates from the player response. Some streams are signed and time bounded.

extractEndScreens.title: Extract end screens and cards
extractEndScreens.description: Pull end screen elements and info cards. Useful for cross promotion analysis on creator networks.

region.title: Region (gl)
region.description: Two letter country code passed as gl. Affects which results YouTube returns and which currency monetary fields show.

language.title: Interface language (hl)
language.description: Two letter language code passed as hl. Affects which language YouTube renders metadata in.

dedupe.title: Deduplicate across runs
dedupe.description: Skip video IDs already pushed in previous runs. Turn off to refresh stale rows.

concurrency.title: Concurrency
concurrency.description: Number of pages processed in parallel. Three to five is safe. Higher values trigger consent walls and rate limits.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy configuration
proxyConfiguration.description: Apify proxy. Residential is required because YouTube serves bot challenges to datacenter IPs on most high-traffic videos.
